attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post, rebutting Noah Smith.

semantics.note: The core historical assertions are kept, and the hedge on subsidy vs profit is preserved. The proposition leaves out the firm claim that Smith picked the quarter post hoc, but the contract restores it.

contract.note: Reading spring quarter as calendar Q2 fits the April–June references. Treating the profit comparison as a hedge is fair. Whether reduced ramp-up charges count as a subsidy depends on interpretation, and the contract says so.

evidence.note: May 21 report of a SpaceX discount for May–June as the deal ramps up. It gives no value and does not show a concession beyond capacity-proportional pricing, so it neither proves nor rules out a material one-time subsidy.
June 30 commentary that tokenmaxxing appears to be dying out. It is tentative, with no measured series, so it cannot establish a peak during the quarter.

reviews.rationale: A discount for May–June was reported, but its value, its baseline and whether it is a true subsidy are not established. The packet has no measured tokenmaxxing peak, does not identify the Chinese advances, and has no evidence on Smith's post-hoc selection. The firm components cannot be confirmed or ruled out from this evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet assertion. Krugman is cited only as an example.

semantics.note: Adding 'public' is a minor gloss, and dropping 'for many reasons' does not change the commitment.

contract.note: The plain reading (substantially growing negative sentiment plus organized opposition, US-centred, H1 2026) is ordinary and not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: Gallup survey fielded in May 2026, published July 28 (before the evaluation date). The share saying AI does more harm than good rose from 31% to 39%, and trust fell.
Q1 2026: active opposition groups more than doubled, and the number of blocked or delayed projects hit a record. Organized opposition with real consequences.
June 13 report on the same findings, citing several concerns. It is not independent of e2.
Confirms worsening US/UK sentiment but not a worldwide trend. Fieldwork dates are unclear.

reviews.rationale: Comparable Gallup polling shows US negative sentiment rising year over year. Records show organized data-center opposition sharply up in Q1 2026, over several concerns. That meets the plain-reading support condition for the US. Public First's finding that the backlash is not global limits breadth but does not contradict the US-centred reading.

attribution.note: Marcus states the NYT report in his own words and builds on it ('the delay reflects a lack of confidence'), so he endorses it.

semantics.note: A tentative preference as of late June. 'Next year' correctly means 2027.

contract.note: It correctly separates a leaning from a final decision or the actual listing date.

evidence.note: June 25 coverage cites the Times and three people in the deliberations: OpenAI was considering waiting until 2027. It derives from the same Times reporting.

reviews.rationale: Contemporaneous reporting, sourced to people involved in the deliberations, says OpenAI favoured postponing its IPO to 2027 as of June 25. The contract accepts attributed reporting when internal records are unavailable. No evidence contradicts the reported leaning.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet assertion. The zerohedge/Bloomberg post is cited as illustration.

semantics.note: 'Market traction' is a minor gloss on 'traction'. 'Fast' is preserved as 'rapidly'.

contract.note: Using usage on the OpenRouter platform, which Marcus himself cited, with a June-to-date window is an ordinary reading. The contract also notes the limits of measuring by token share.

evidence.note: OpenRouter's analysis of its own request logs through June 14 (published June 30), measuring third-party model usage. DeepSeek went from about 5% in Feb–Mar to nearly 20% by early June, and other Chinese labs also gained share.

reviews.rationale: Platform logs show Chinese-model token share rising sharply within a few months and into June: DeepSeek roughly quadrupled from its low, and Xiaomi, Minimax and Tencent also gained. That meets 'gaining traction, fast' on the named platform. Global revenue or user share is not established, and the claim did not require it.
